title: Free compute for agents: every API provider, its key page and its quirks
subtitle: Twelve providers, one page each: where to make the key, what to send, what will trip you.
intro: I wanted a coding agent that can run on free tiers before it touches a paid plan. So I opened an account on every API provider that gives something away, made a key, and sent one real request through each.

This page is what I wrote down: the page where the key is created, the base URL, the header, the odd settings, and the one thing that bit me. Limits change often, so treat each free tier line as dated 3 November 2026 and check the provider before you rely on it.

providers.name: Google AI Studio (Gemini)
providers.tagline: The easiest start: a Google login and a key.
providers.authHeader: x-goog-api-key: <key> (the OpenAI-compatible path under /v1beta/openai/ takes Authorization: Bearer)
settings: Free tier needs an active project; moving to paid Tier 1 is instant from the billing page
Per-model limits are only shown on aistudio.google.com/rate-limit while logged in
Several keys in one Google Cloud project share one quota
providers.freeTier: Free Flash and Flash-Lite models with per-project request limits; exact numbers are shown only in the logged-in console.
providers.gotcha: Free-tier prompts may be used for training and human review, and the Pro preview model refuses free keys.

providers.name: OpenCode Zen
providers.tagline: Free open models, but only through the official client.
settings: Free models answer only the official OpenCode client; a plain OpenAI client gets a 429 FreeUsageLimitError on the first call
One model is blocked by region (403 RegionError from France)
Sign in with GitHub or Google, then create the key in the console
providers.freeTier: Several models carry a -free suffix; the docs state no published cap.
providers.gotcha: The 429 is a client fingerprint gate, not a quota, so it looks like you are rate limited when you are not.

providers.name: Groq
providers.tagline: Very fast, with tight per-minute token caps.
settings: Reasoning models reject the developer role; send system instead
One oversized prompt returns 413 because of the per-minute input cap
Limits are per organization and per model
providers.freeTier: Roughly 30 requests per minute, 1,000 per day and 8,000 tokens per minute on the main chat models.
providers.gotcha: Agent prompts of about 8,600 tokens exceed the free input cap on the Qwen model, so use it for short direct prompts.

providers.name: Cerebras
providers.tagline: Generous measured limits and very high speed.
settings: Create the key from the API keys section after signing in
Model availability changes; check the deprecation page before pinning a name
providers.freeTier: Free access with per-minute and per-day token buckets; the headers I measured were higher than the documented free trial figures.
providers.gotcha: The headers I saw match no documented tier, so do not plan around them.

providers.name: Mistral
providers.tagline: Free plan exists, but you must switch it on.
settings: Activate the free Experiment plan in the console first
Listing models works without the plan, which makes a key look healthy
providers.freeTier: Experiment plan with per-workspace request and token limits; figures are not published on the docs.
providers.gotcha: Until the plan is activated every chat call returns 429 code 1300 while the key still lists models.

providers.name: Cohere
settings: reasoning_effort accepts only none or high
Strip unsupported OpenAI parameters such as store
The developer role is accepted as system
providers.freeTier: Trial key: 20 chat calls per minute and 1,000 calls per month.
providers.gotcha: The monthly cap counts calls, so one giant prompt costs the same as a tiny one.

providers.name: NVIDIA NIM
providers.tagline: A big catalogue behind one key.
settings: Sign in to build.nvidia.com and generate the key from any model page
One account-level rate ceiling, unpublished; community reports say about 40 requests per minute
providers.freeTier: Free developer access with a request rate limit and no published token budget.
providers.gotcha: About 85 models are listed but not all are callable; one returned 404 for my account.

providers.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
providers.tagline: Neuron budget with the account id in the URL.
providers.authHeader: Authorization: Bearer <API token with Workers AI permission>
settings: Account id is required in the path; a generic base URL fails
Create an API token with the Workers AI permission, not a global key
Omit reasoning_effort for the Qwen model
providers.freeTier: 10,000 Neurons per day, reset at 00:00 UTC, with 300 requests per minute on text generation.
providers.gotcha: Paid-only models error on the free plan even though they appear in the catalogue.

providers.name: Hugging Face Inference Providers
providers.tagline: A router to many hosts, billed in credits.
settings: Create a fine-grained token with the inference permission
Credits are per account; PRO includes a small monthly amount
providers.freeTier: None that works for chat: free accounts have no included credits.
models: Pick after buying credits or upgrading to PRO
providers.gotcha: The models list shows over a hundred models, yet every chat call returns HTTP 402 on a free account.

providers.name: Vercel AI Gateway
providers.tagline: One gateway, free credit behind a card.
settings: A credit card on file is required to unlock the free credit
Create the key from the AI Gateway section of your team dashboard
GET /v1/credits shows the balance without spending anything
providers.freeTier: A small monthly credit, released only after card verification.
models: Any model in the gateway catalogue, once the credit is unlocked
providers.gotcha: Chat returns 403 customer_verification_required until a card is added, and buying credits ends the free credit.

providers.name: xAI Grok
providers.tagline: Prepaid credit; no free pool confirmed.
settings: Keys must be created in the xAI console; keys from other apps are rejected
Limits are per model and depend on spend tier
providers.freeTier: No free pool confirmed; usage draws on prepaid credit.
providers.gotcha: A key obtained through a third party app is not an xAI API key and fails authentication.

providers.name: OpenRouter
providers.tagline: The :free models, with limits tied to your credit history.
settings: Only model ids ending in :free count against the free pool
Adding credits changes your daily free limit
providers.freeTier: 20 requests per minute and 50 per day on :free models; 1,000 per day after buying at least 10 credits.
providers.gotcha: A mid-stream limit error arrives as an SSE chunk with finish_reason error, not as an HTTP status.

providers.name: Claude Max (subscription aside)
providers.tagline: Not an API key: a plan with a shared pool.
providers.baseUrl: none (sign in with the official client)
settings: One pool shared by chat, Desktop and Claude Code
A rolling five hour session plus a weekly window
providers.freeTier: Not free; usage is a percentage of the plan.
providers.gotcha: The usage endpoint rate limits quickly, so read the percentage the client already shows.

providers.name: Codex (subscription aside)
providers.baseUrl: none (sign in with the official client)
settings: Rolling five hour and weekly windows
providers.freeTier: Included with a ChatGPT plan; limits are percentages.
providers.gotcha: Treat the shown percentage as the only truth; there is no per-token figure.

providers.name: Local inference
providers.tagline: The one that never runs out.
providers.authHeader: none, or a token you set
settings: Any OpenAI-compatible server works
providers.gotcha: It is free per token and costs you in speed and setup.

closing: If you start today: take Gemini and Cerebras for volume, Groq for speed on short prompts, Cohere for a monthly trickle, and keep local inference as the floor. Skip anything that asks for a card until you need it.
